title: Throughput obligation matrix and escalation scripting for Dedicated capacity contracts
creator: Asha Menon
description: Define a precise, auditable SLA for Dedicated capacity throughput commitments, including an errors-and-credit computation, explicit measurement windows, and scripted escalation paths for legal/ops. This ticket produces: a measurement spec, credit computation formula (with examples), contract-ready language snippets, and an operations playbook for escalation and automated credit issuance.
background: Customers want predictable serving capacity for reserved GPU pools. Prior artifacts cover many SLA shapes but lack a single, testable obligation matrix that ties quantile measurements to credit tiers and prescribes automated remediation triggers for autoscaling and fleet controls. This doc balances legal simplicity with operational fidelity.
measurement_spec: Primary metric: Committed Throughput (CT) expressed in tokens-per-minute (TPM) measured per customer reservation. Measurement window: rolling 30-day window with a 5-minute aggregation bucket. Service-level condition: CT is considered met when the 99th percentile of 5-minute TPM across the 30-day window >= contracted CT. Secondary guardrail: median (p50) 5-minute TPM must be >= 80% of CT for sustained degradation detection. Downtime and scheduled maintenance windows are excluded by notice-based blackout windows recorded in the metrics system.
credit_formula: Credit calculation model: daily shortfall S_d = max(0, CT - observed_99pct_TPM_d). Convert token shortfall to credit dollars using effective price-per-token (P). Daily credit C_d = min(cap_daily, S_d * P). Monthly credit = sum(C_d) across rolling 30 days, capped at 20% of monthly committed spend. Example: CT=1,000,000 TPM, P= $0.0000005/token, observed_99pct=800,000 TPM -> S_d=200,000 tokens -> C_d = 200,000 * 0.0000005 = $100 (subject to caps). Credits issued automatically when monthly credit exceeds $500 or when cumulative credits reach 5% of monthly spend, whichever comes first.
contract_language: Suggested plain-language clause to include in Dedicated agreements: 'Redwood guarantees a committed throughput (CT) measured in tokens-per-minute as specified in Exhibit A. CT compliance is evaluated using the 99th percentile of 5-minute aggregation buckets over a 30-day rolling window, excluding scheduled maintenance windows notified at least 72 hours in advance. If Redwood fails to deliver the committed CT, Customer is eligible for service credits calculated per the credit schedule in Exhibit B. Credits are Redwood’s sole and exclusive remedy for throughput degradation and will not exceed 20% of the affected monthly commitment.' Include optional escalation clause: 'For failures resulting in cumulative credits exceeding 10% of monthly commitment, Redwood will trigger a priority incident and propose a remediation plan within 24 hours.'
autoscale_policy_summary: Autoscaler interlock rules for Dedicated reservations: 1) Baseline buffer: keep 10% headroom (idle capacity) per reservation to absorb spikes without preemption. 2) Burst policy: allow 30% short-term burst for up to 10 minutes with usage-tagging for accounting. 3) Scale-up grace: minimize false positives by requiring 3 consecutive aggregation buckets (5-minute each) before permanent scale-up. 4) Scale-down cool-off: wait 20 minutes after scale-up or observed load drop before deprovisioning GPUs. 5) Failure fallback: if autoscaler cannot meet sustained demand for >15 minutes, auto-trigger a degraded-priority route that shifts traffic to a lower-cost compatible model variant and logs an incident. These policies are tunable per-customer in reservation profiles.
fleet_controls: Allocation and preemption model: reservations are mapped to rings with explicit priority tags. During capacity pressure, autopreemption respects customer priority and negotiated preemption windows. Overcommit guardrail: system will not overcommit more than 12% of total cluster capacity for Dedicated reservations. Preemption notice: automatic 2-minute warning to in-flight requests with graceful degradation attempt via function call fallback. Operator tooling: console exposes per-reservation live headroom, predicted exhaustion ETA (based on trailing 1-hour usage), and a one-click emergency bump to temporary burst capacity (billed at premium).
acceptance_criteria: Measurement spec implemented in metrics pipeline with 5-minute buckets and 99th percentile query validated against synthetic load
Credit calculator script added to billing pipeline with sample outputs matching provided examples
Contract language approved by legal and appended to Dedicated contract templates
Autoscaler interlock rules implemented in staging and validated with chaos tests (scale-up/down, preemption scenarios)
Ops runbook created with scripted escalation emails and Slack workflows for >10% monthly credit events
decisions: Use tokens-per-minute as primary unit to keep cost/credit math model-aligned with API pricing
Use 99th percentile over rolling 30 days to make the SLA tolerant to short transients while protecting customers from sustained degradation
Cap monthly credits at 20% of committed spend to limit financial exposure while offering meaningful remediation
Automate credit issuance above small thresholds to reduce churn and manual billing overhead
